credit_metrics.text: EBITDA increased by {{ebitda.change@FY2025}} to {{ebitda@FY2025}}, and operating profit rose by {{operating_profit.change@FY2025}} to {{operating_profit@FY2025}} despite higher depreciation and impairment charges.

Total debt was stable at {{total_debt@FY2025}} and net debt at {{net_debt@FY2025}}, so the rise in EBITDA brought net leverage down by {{net_leverage.change@FY2025}} to {{net_leverage@FY2025}} and gross leverage to {{gross_leverage@FY2025}}.

FFO rose by {{ffo.change@FY2025}} to {{ffo@FY2025}}, lifting FFO to debt by {{ffo_to_debt.change@FY2025}} to {{ffo_to_debt@FY2025}}, and interest coverage improved by {{interest_coverage.change@FY2025}} to {{interest_coverage@FY2025}}.

Free cash flow increased by {{fcf.change@FY2025}} to {{fcf@FY2025}}, taking FCF to debt to {{fcf_to_debt@FY2025}}, while capex intensity eased by {{capex_intensity.change@FY2025}} to {{capex_intensity@FY2025}}.

liquidity_funding.text: Cash and cash-like investments fell by {{cash_like.change@FY2025}} to {{cash_like@FY2025}}, taking cash liquidity to revenue down by {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.change@FY2025}} to {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue@FY2025}}.
The TAV group's guarantee of part of the Antalya concession bank loan no longer exists at year-end following the refinancing of that loan.

peer_positioning.text: Groupe ADP has the weakest EBITDA margin of the airport peers ({{ebitda_margin.peer_rank@FY2025}}), at {{ebitda_margin@FY2025}} against a median of {{ebitda_margin.peer_median@FY2025}}.

Leverage is the weakest in the group, with net leverage ranking {{net_leverage.peer_rank@FY2025}} against a median of {{net_leverage.peer_median@FY2025}} and gross leverage also last ({{gross_leverage.peer_rank@FY2025}}).

Cash generation and coverage sit behind the group as well, with FFO to debt against a median of {{ffo_to_debt.peer_median@FY2025}} and interest coverage against {{interest_coverage.peer_median@FY2025}}, while capex intensity sits in the middle of the group.

snapshot.text: Groupe ADP, the Paris airport group that also consolidates TAV Airports, grew revenue by {{revenue.change@FY2025}} to {{revenue@FY2025}} in FY2025, with the Ankara Esenboga concession renewal entering service during the year.

The EBITDA margin widened by {{ebitda_margin.change@FY2025}} to {{ebitda_margin@FY2025}} and net leverage fell by {{net_leverage.change@FY2025}} to {{net_leverage@FY2025}}, helped by broadly unchanged net debt of {{net_debt@FY2025}}.

The point to watch is cash liquidity, which fell by {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.change@FY2025}} to {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue@FY2025}} of revenue, the weakest of the airport peers ({{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.peer_rank@FY2025}}).
